items.prose: Aged Canada balsam optical cement bonding the ninety-degree erector prisms crystallized into a web of micro-fractures. Light transmission dropped by 55%, tinting the surface observation field an opaque muddy amber.

Extreme temperature differential between the -35°C blizzard exterior mast and +25°C bunker air created intense thermal shear stress. The synthetic epoxy bond between the crown and dense flint elements cleaved with an audible snap, producing total internal reflection glare.

Fungal hyphae of *Aspergillus niger* colonized the moist interface between lens elements. The metabolic oxalic acid etched permanent dendritic tree-like grooves into the lead flint glass, scattering spotlight beams into blinding halos.

Maintenance crews sealed the mast viewing port using household acetoxy-cure silicone sealant. The outgassed acetic acid vapor reacted with the anti-reflection coating on the inner lens surface, depositing a milky, un-cleanable white chemical haze.

Windblown volcanic ash scoured the 1/4-wave magnesium fluoride anti-reflection coating off the objective lens. Flare and internal ghost reflections tripled, blinding sentries during dawn and dusk surveillance.

High-intensity gamma radiation (cumulative 120 Gy) generated color-center electron traps in the non-stabilized optical crown elements. The glass darkened from water-white to dark molasses brown, rendering the periscope useless for night viewing.

Deterioration of the Schrader charging valve allowed dry argon gas to bleed out of the four-meter optical tube. Moist bunker air infiltrated, condensing droplets of water on the internal reticle plate whenever outside temperatures dropped below freezing.

Airborne hydrogen sulfide from geothermal steam vents penetrated pinholes in the silicon monoxide protective overcoat. The front-surface silver mirror tarnished into black silver sulfide, reducing reflectivity from 98% to less than 35%.
